submission.justification: Based on comprehensive simulations across all three candidate materials and plate thicknesses from 2-10 mm, Absorber-F1 with 5 mm plate thickness delivers the best energy resolution of 3.174% at 100 GeV. This represents approximately 20% better resolution than Absorber-F3 (best at 3.934% with 4 mm plates) and 37% better than Absorber-F2 (best at 5.004% with 6 mm plates). All three materials are listed as valid candidates in the project specifications, can be machined to required tolerances, and are compatible with the mechanical support design. The 5 mm thickness is well within the 2-10 mm constraint and matches the thickness from the 2025 simulation summary, providing continuity with previous studies. This configuration achieves the primary goal of best possible energy resolution while meeting all stated constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5 mm achieves 3.174% energy resolution, which is the best among all tested configurations (24 simulations covering all three materials at various thicknesses)

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is explicitly listed as a candidate material in candidate_specs.md as 'dense alloy with a short radiation length'

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: All three candidate materials including Absorber-F1 are listed as valid options in the project specifications. No document excludes any candidate on activation or radiation safety grounds. If hands-on maintenance were not possible with F1, it would not be included as a candidate option.
Recommended thickness of 5 mm is within the specified range of 2-10 mm
